run.question: We got a customer complaint about slow response times in Europe. The customer mentioned seeing request ID REQ-EU-8K4M2 in their error page. Find what happened with this request and which service had the issue.

report.summary: I could not tie request REQ-EU-8K4M2 to any service: no document containing that identifier exists in the only log store I could search (Elasticsearch/OpenSearch, all 1620 indices, full 24h window), and the two sources that could hold per-request latency and error data - Jaeger traces and the Prometheus span/RPC metrics - were unreachable through the provided tools for every attempt (SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE). What the reachable telemetry does show is a benign, uniform picture: the Elasticsearch corpus in the window is 162 documents, all level INFO, all message "Request completed successfully", with response_time_ms identical at 150 for min-less avg and max across all six regions including eu-central and eu-west (27 docs each), so no European latency deviation or error severity is visible there. On the Kubernetes side all 21 otel-demo deployments were 1/1 ready and all 22 otel-demo pods Running/Ready at query time; the only non-application failure marks are on observability components (prometheus-readonly-proxy nginx and kube-state-metrics), and every application container's last termination is reason Unknown/exit 255 at 04:23:42Z, i.e. a node/sandbox teardown, not OOMKilled or Evicted. The application logs I read (checkout newest 100 lines, quote, shipping, email, product-catalog) contain no error lines and no request identifiers. A genuine defect I did observe is that the otel-collector's own telemetry is misconfigured (OTLP gRPC export to port 4318, an HTTP port), producing continuous "failed to upload metrics ... frame header looked like an HTTP/1.1 header" errors, and its logs pipeline exports only to debug, which is why request-level application logs never reach OpenSearch; neither of these ties to the customer's EU request, so I do not name a root cause and record the identification as unresolved.

claims.text: In the full 24h authorized window across all 1620 matched indices, Elasticsearch holds 162 documents, all of level INFO with message "Request completed successfully"; response_time_ms max = 150 and avg = 150.0, and the region breakdown is six regions with 27 documents each (ap-northeast, ap-south, eu-central, eu-west, us-east, us-west). No ERROR/WARN level document appears in that corpus.

The Elasticsearch document schema of the app-185-geo-* indices has only @timestamp, level, message, region, response_time_ms and service; there is no request-id or trace-id field, so a customer request identifier can only appear inside the free-text message field.

All 21 otel-demo deployments reported 1 desired, 1 ready, 1 available and 1 updated replica at the time of the query (ad, cart, checkout, currency, email, flagd, frontend, frontend-proxy, image-provider, jaeger, kube-state-metrics, load-generator, otel-collector, payment, product-catalog, prometheus, prometheus-readonly-proxy, quote, recommendation, shipping, valkey-cart).

All 22 otel-demo pods were phase Running and Ready. Every application container's last termination is reason "Unknown" with exitCode 255, finishedAt 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z, restartCount 1; the exceptions are kube-state-metrics (reason Error, exitCode 1, finishedAt 04:24:17Z, restartCount 2) and prometheus-readonly-proxy nginx (reason Error, exitCode 1, finishedAt 04:24:10Z, restartCount 3). No container shows reason OOMKilled or Evicted.

The single node opspilot-m1-control-plane was created 2026-11-20T16:31:42Z and is Ready (no MemoryPressure, DiskPressure or PIDPressure), and the otel-demo pods were created from 2026-11-20T16:32:06Z onward, so the observable object history starts roughly 12 hours into the authorized window.

The previous prometheus-readonly-proxy nginx container died with "[emerg] host not found in upstream \"prometheus:9090\" in /etc/nginx/nginx.conf:22" at 2026-11-21T04:24:10Z, and its pod shows 5 readiness-probe failures (dial tcp 10.244.0.2:8080: connect: connection refused, 04:23:51-04:24:34Z) and 4 BackOff events for container nginx (04:23:53-04:24:14Z).

The otel-demo ConfigMap "otel-collector" sets the collector's own telemetry metrics reader to a periodic OTLP exporter with endpoint otel-collector:4318 and protocol grpc, and its logs pipeline lists only the debug exporter even though an opensearch exporter (endpoint http://opensearch:9200, logs_index otel) is defined but not attached to any pipeline.

The otel-collector logs repeat "failed to upload metrics: reader collect and export timeout: rpc error: code = Unavailable ... error reading server preface: http2: failed reading the frame payload: http2: frame too large, note that the frame header looked like an HTTP/1.1 header" every 10 seconds, covering 2026-11-21T03:48:22Z-03:54:22Z in the previous container and 04:40:02Z-04:46:02Z in the current container, against address 10.96.247.55:4318 / ServerName otel-collector:4318.

The otel-collector debug exporter was continuously emitting batches ("Metrics", "Traces", "Logs" records with span and data-point counts) between 2026-11-21T04:45:48Z and 04:46:10Z, showing that application telemetry was still being received and processed at the end of the window.

The prometheus-server container was accepting remote-write traffic through the end of the window, logging write_handler warnings ("Error on ingesting out-of-order exemplars", num_dropped 2-10) at roughly 10-second cadence up to 2026-11-21T04:45:49Z; its only startup errors were API-server connection refusals at 04:23:51Z.
The jaeger all-in-one container logged health state "ready", "Query server started" on [::]:16686/[::]:16685 and a connected agent-collector channel at 2026-11-21T04:23:48Z.

The newest 100 checkout log lines (2026-11-21T04:26:33Z-04:45:54Z) contain only successful PlaceOrder / "payment went through" / "order confirmation email sent" entries with no error or timeout lines, and contain no request identifier field.

The frontend's previous container logged repeated "Error: 14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 10.96.220.188:8080" at 2026-11-20T16:33:30Z-16:33:34Z, i.e. during its own startup right after the app was created, and its current container has only startup lines.

Every fault-injection flag in the flagd-config ConfigMap (productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adManualGc, adHighCpu, adFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, imageSlowLoad) has defaultVariant "off" as read; flagd's own logs contain only startup and shutdown lines from 2026-11-20T16:33:08Z and 2026-11-21T04:23:49Z, with no flag-change or evaluation-error lines.

The repeated Jaeger and Prometheus SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE failures are more likely an access-path problem on the observability read path (for example the prometheus-readonly-proxy, whose nginx.conf is mounted from a Secret that cannot be read) than the backends being down, because the jaeger container reported ready at 04:23:48Z and prometheus-server was still ingesting remote writes at 04:45:49Z. This is not proven.

The otel-collector telemetry misconfiguration (OTLP gRPC export to otel-collector:4318, an OTLP/HTTP port) explains the continuous "frame header looked like an HTTP/1.1 header" upload failures for the collector's own self-metrics only; it does not by itself explain any customer-facing latency, and no evidence connects it to slow responses in Europe.

A flagd-injected latency or failure (imageSlowLoad, adHighCpu, kafkaQueueProblems, paymentFailure and similar) could in principle produce slow requests, but at read time every flag's defaultVariant is "off" and no flag change appears in flagd's logs, so this remains an unverified candidate rather than an observed cause.

Rejected: OOMKill or eviction caused the incident. No pod has an OOMKilled or Evicted reason; every application container's last termination is reason Unknown with exitCode 255 all at the same instant 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z, which is a sandbox/node teardown pattern, and the current pods are Running/Ready.

Rejected: a European-region latency or error problem is visible in the searchable logs. The window's whole Elasticsearch corpus is 162 INFO documents with message "Request completed successfully" and max = avg = 150 ms for response_time_ms, with eu-central and eu-west each holding 27 identical documents like the other four regions.

Against treating any single pod as the culprit: all 22 otel-demo pods were Running and Ready, all 21 deployments had 1/1 available replicas, and the ReplicaSet owner chain is intact (each ReplicaSet owned by its Deployment, e.g. checkout-6578865d87 -> checkout, frontend-proxy-844799bcdb -> frontend-proxy, prometheus-9bc78b5f7 -> prometheus), so no workload-level failure was observed.

gaps: No document containing REQ-EU-8K4M2 was returned: a match_phrase query on message over index pattern '*' (1620 indices) for the full window 2026-11-20T04:46:11Z-2026-11-21T04:46:11Z returned no documents, and a query_string search for the same string matched only 54 background documents that do not contain the identifier. The identifier is therefore not resolvable to a trace, service, region or time through Elasticsearch.

Jaeger (traces_search, traces_search_by_tags, traces_query_trace_by_id, traces_list_services, traces_list_operations) returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE on every attempt (04:46:13Z, 04:46:29Z, 04:46:49Z, 04:47:33Z, 04:48:22Z, 04:49:06Z), so per-request trace data for REQ-EU-8K4M2 could not be read and no span, operation or parent-child edge can be attributed.

Prometheus (get_metric_names, get_all_labels, execute_prometheus_instant_query, list_prometheus_rules, get_prometheus_target, metrics_range_query) returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE on every attempt (04:46:15Z-04:49:06Z), so traces_span_metrics_calls_total, rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count, rpc_server_duration_milliseconds_bucket, http_server_request_duration_seconds_count and app_payment_transactions_total could not be evaluated; error rates, latency and label coverage remain unknown rather than zero.

Per-request application logs are not in Elasticsearch because the otel-collector ConfigMap's logs pipeline exports only to the debug exporter, not to the defined opensearch exporter; therefore absence of the request identifier in the log store says nothing about whether the request was served or how slow it was.

Container restarts at about 2026-11-21T04:07Z (graceful shutdown of the previous container instances) and 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z (sandbox teardown) destroyed log coverage beyond one previous instance; for most pods only 16:32Z-04:07Z of the 24h window plus post-04:23Z is retained, and object history starts at node creation 2026-11-20T16:31:42Z.

The prometheus-readonly-proxy nginx configuration is mounted from a Secret (secret name redacted) which cannot be read, so I could not verify which upstream and port the gateway's Prometheus read path uses or why it still fails after the proxy became Ready.

A level!=INFO query over all indices in the window returned nothing, and networkpolicies returned no objects; an empty result only records that those queries matched nothing, it is not proof that no error-level log or policy existed.

No change history is available (change_history integration is not integrated in this Run), so the two cluster-wide restart waves and the prometheus/otel-collector ReplicaSet pairs created at 16:32Z and 16:33Z cannot be attributed to a specific change.
next_steps: Retrieve the trace for REQ-EU-8K4M2 directly from Jaeger (jaeger-query:16686) once the read path is reachable, and compare the slow span's service/operation against its parent to locate the latency source.

Evaluate traces_span_metrics_calls_total by service_name, span_name and status_code plus rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_bucket for the 04:00-04:46Z period once Prometheus is reachable, to identify which operation carried elevated latency or errors.
Run the existing CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh rule expression (checkout PlaceOrder server spans, status_code STATUS_CODE_ERROR vs total) for the window to test whether checkout was failing.

Fix the otel-collector ConfigMap telemetry setting: export the collector's own metrics to gRPC port 4317 instead of otel-collector:4318, which is an OTLP/HTTP port, and add the opensearch exporter to the logs pipeline if request-level application logs are meant to be searchable.

Inspect the prometheus-readonly-proxy Secret nginx.conf (cannot be read here) and the deployment's 3 restarts with exit 1 at 04:24Z, since that proxy is the read path to Prometheus and its upstream resolution failed with 'host not found in upstream prometheus:9090'.

view.cannot_prove: This is the state at the moment of the query only: it cannot prove which indices, fields or document counts existed during the incident window, nor that any document lies in that window. A field that is mapped is not proof that documents carry it.

A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind.

global: {}
receivers:
- name: opspilot
  webhook_configs:
  - http_config:
      authorization:
        [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL] /etc/alertmanager/opspilot/token
        type: Bearer [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]: 0
    send_resolved: true
    url: http://opspilot-web:8080/intake/alertmanager
- name: opspilot-self
route:
  group_by:
  - alertname
  - namespace
  - service
  group_interval: 1m
  group_wait: 10s
  receiver: opspilot
  repeat_interval: 1h
  routes:
  - matchers:
    - opspilot_self="true"
    receiver: opspilot-self
templates: []

data.relay:
connectors:
  spanmetrics: {}
exporters:
  debug: {}
  opensearch:
    http:
      endpoint: http://opensearch:9200
      tls:
        insecure: true
    logs_index: otel
  otlp:
    endpoint: jaeger-collector:4317
    tls:
      insecure: true
  otlphttp/prometheus:
    auth:
      [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL] basicauth/prometheus
    endpoint: http://prometheus:9090/api/v1/otlp
    tls:
      insecure: true
extensions:
  basicauth/prometheus:
    client_auth:
      [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL] ${env:PROMETHEUS_COLLECTOR_PASSWORD}
      username: collector
  health_check:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:13133
processors:
  batch: {}
  k8sattributes:
    extract:
      metadata:
      - k8s.namespace.name
      - k8s.deployment.name
      - k8s.statefulset.name
      - k8s.daemonset.name
      - k8s.cronjob.name
      - k8s.job.name
      - k8s.node.name
      - k8s.pod.name
      - k8s.pod.uid
      - k8s.pod.start_time
    passthrough: false
    pod_association:
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.ip
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.uid
    - sources:
      - from: connection
  memory_limiter:
    check_interval: 5s
    limit_percentage: 80
    spike_limit_percentage: 25
  resource:
    attributes:
    - action: insert
      from_attribute: k8s.pod.uid
      key: service.instance.id
  transform:
    error_mode: ignore
    trace_statements:
    - context: span
      statements:
      - replace_pattern(name, "\\?.*", "")
      - replace_match(name, "GET /api/products/*", "GET /api/products/{productId}")

  httpcheck/frontend-proxy:
    targets:
    - endpoint: http://frontend-proxy:8080

groups:
- name: opspilot-lab
  rules:
  - alert: CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value | humanizePercentage }} of checkout PlaceOrder server
        spans ended in error over the last 5 minutes.'
      summary: checkout PlaceOrder error ratio above 50%
    expr: |
      label_replace(label_replace(
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])))
        /
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder"}[5m])))
      , "namespace", "$1", "k8s_namespace_name", "(.*)"), "service", "$1", "service_name", "(.*)")
      > 0.5
    for: 2m
    labels:
      cluster: opspilot-m1
      opspilot_integration_id: m0-otel-20260909
      severity: critical
- name: opspilot-self
  rules:
  - alert: OpsPilotAgentAbsent
    annotations:
      description: role {{ $labels.role }} ({{ $labels.instance }}) has not answered
        /metrics for 2 minutes.
      summary: an OpsPilot health listener is down or the worker is not scraped
    expr: up{job="opspilot"} == 0 or absent(up{job="opspilot",role="worker"})
    for: 2m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
  - alert: OpsPilotModelCallsFailing
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value }} consecutive model calls failed on {{ $labels.instance
        }}.'
      summary: OpsPilot model calls are failing
    expr: opspilot_model_consecutive_failures >= 2
    for: 1m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
